accepted.s: Which of the following Gupta rulers was the first to adopt the title ‘Maharajadhiraja’?
accepted.x: Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler to assume the imperial title ‘Maharajadhiraja’. Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha used only the title ‘Maharaja’.
accepted.tq: Use the title-to-ruler association and distinguish the first adopter from earlier rulers.
accepted.sec: Titles and epithets → ruler (Kaviraja, Vikramaditya, Maharajadhiraja, Lichchhavi-dauhitra, Prithivyah Pratham Veer, Napoleon of India)

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the titles of the early Gupta rulers:
1. Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha used the title ‘Maharaja’.
2. Chandragupta I was the first Gupta ruler to assume ‘Maharajadhiraja’.
3. Kumaragupta I was known by the title ‘Mahendraditya’.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Sri Gupta and Ghatotkacha used ‘Maharaja’, Chandragupta I first adopted ‘Maharajadhiraja’, and Kumaragupta I bore the title ‘Mahendraditya’.
accepted.tq: Check each title against its ruler before selecting the combined code.
accepted.sec: Titles and epithets → ruler (Kaviraja, Vikramaditya, Maharajadhiraja, Lichchhavi-dauhitra, Prithivyah Pratham Veer, Napoleon of India)

accepted.s: The title ‘Mahendraditya’ is associated with which Gupta ruler?
accepted.x: Kumaragupta I assumed the title ‘Mahendraditya’.
accepted.tq: Test a less commonly recalled ruler-title pair against nearby Gupta rulers.
accepted.sec: Titles and epithets → ruler (Kaviraja, Vikramaditya, Maharajadhiraja, Lichchhavi-dauhitra, Prithivyah Pratham Veer, Napoleon of India)

accepted.s: Which one of the following was NOT a common imperial title used by Gupta rulers?
accepted.x: Parameshvara, Maharajadhiraja and Paramabhattaraka were imperial titles associated with the Gupta tradition. ‘Dharmamahamatra’ was an administrative designation associated with the Mauryan period, not a common Gupta imperial title.
accepted.tq: Find the outsider among closely related imperial titles.
accepted.sec: Titles and epithets → ruler (Kaviraja, Vikramaditya, Maharajadhiraja, Lichchhavi-dauhitra, Prithivyah Pratham Veer, Napoleon of India)

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the treatment of the southern rulers defeated by Samudragupta?
o: They were defeated, released and reinstated as tributaries.
They were allowed to retain independence without accepting Gupta suzerainty.
They were replaced by Gupta governors in every southern kingdom.
They were permanently annexed into the Gupta Empire.
accepted.x: Samudragupta followed the policy of grahana-moksha-anugraha in the south: the rulers were captured, released and restored as tributaries rather than being permanently annexed.
accepted.tq: Apply the north-versus-south policy distinction to a conquest scenario.
accepted.sec: Samudragupta's campaigns - north vs south policy, southern kings defeated → kingdom (Vishnugopa, Hastivarman, Mahendra, Swamidatta), outcomes

accepted.s: The policy of grahana-moksha-anugraha followed by Samudragupta in the Dakshinapatha campaign means:
o: Capture, release and favour towards defeated rulers
Defeat, annexation and imposition of Gupta administration
accepted.x: Grahana-moksha-anugraha literally conveys the policy of capture, release and favour. The southern kings were restored as tributaries after accepting Gupta suzerainty.
accepted.tq: Decode the technical expression by matching each term with the campaign outcome.
accepted.sec: Samudragupta's campaigns - north vs south policy, southern kings defeated → kingdom (Vishnugopa, Hastivarman, Mahendra, Swamidatta), outcomes

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Samudragupta’s campaigns:
1. The Ganga-Yamuna region in the north was directly annexed.
2. The southern rulers were generally defeated and reinstated as tributaries.
3. Assam, Nepal and Bengal belonged to the group of frontier rulers who paid tribute.
4. The atavika or forest kingdoms of central India were subdued.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. Samudragupta annexed territory in the north, restored southern rulers as tributaries, received tribute from frontier rulers and subdued forest kingdoms.
accepted.tq: Separate the four categories of opponents before choosing the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Samudragupta's campaigns - north vs south policy, southern kings defeated → kingdom (Vishnugopa, Hastivarman, Mahendra, Swamidatta), outcomes

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly identifies the southern king and his kingdom in Samudragupta’s campaign?
accepted.x: Kubera ruled Devarashtra, identified with the southern Vizianagaram region. Dhananjaya was associated with Kusthalapura, Vyaghraraja with Mahakantara and Mantaraja with Kurala.
accepted.tq: Use one exact ruler–kingdom pairing while rejecting reversed associations.

accepted.s: How many kings were defeated and released during Samudragupta’s Dakshinapatha campaign?
accepted.x: The Allahabad Prasasti refers to twelve southern kings who were defeated and subsequently released and reinstated as tributaries.
accepted.tq: Use the campaign number directly and distinguish it from the four categories of opponents.

accepted.s: Which of the following statements regarding Samudragupta’s southern campaign is correct?
o: It extended towards Kanchi, and the defeated rulers were restored as tributaries.
It ended after the conquest of Vengi because the remaining rulers were not encountered.
It was confined to the western coast and was directed mainly against the Sakas.
It extended along the eastern coast up to Kanchi and resulted in permanent annexation of all conquered territories.
accepted.x: The Dakshinapatha campaign proceeded along the eastern coast towards Kanchi. Samudragupta restored the defeated rulers instead of permanently annexing their kingdoms.
accepted.tq: Combine route and outcome to reject the permanent-annexation trap.
accepted.sec: Samudragupta's campaigns - north vs south policy, southern kings defeated → kingdom (Vishnugopa, Hastivarman, Mahendra, Swamidatta), outcomes

accepted.s: Samudragupta celebrated his conquests by performing which ritual?
accepted.x: Samudragupta performed an Ashvamedha to celebrate his military achievements and also issued Ashvamedha coins.

o: The ruler performing a fire sacrifice with a tiger
The ruler receiving tribute from a Roman ambassador
The ruler riding an elephant with a bow
accepted.x: Some coins of Samudragupta depict him playing the veena, reflecting his association with music and culture.

accepted.x: The Buddhist scholar Vasubandhu is mentioned as a minister of Samudragupta. Harisena was his court poet and author of the Allahabad Prasasti.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the minister from the court poet and other Gupta-era literary figures.

accepted.x: The Allahabad or Prayaga Prasasti is a Sanskrit eulogy of Samudragupta’s conquests.

o: Mixed prose and verse in champu style
A copper-plate grant in formal legal prose

accepted.s: Which of the following offices was NOT held by Harisena?
accepted.x: Harisena held the offices of Kumaramatya, Sandhivigrahika and Mahadandanayaka. He was not a Mahamatra of Ashoka, who belonged to an earlier period.
accepted.tq: Reject the office belonging to another imperial administrative system.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about Harisena:
1. He was associated with the court of Samudragupta.
2. He held the offices of Kumaramatya, Sandhivigrahika and Mahadandanayaka.
3. He should be identified without distinction with the later Jain author of the Brihatkatha Kosha.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. The Harisena associated with Samudragupta must not be confused with the later Jain author of the Brihatkatha Kosha.
accepted.tq: Use the confusable-person trap and separate two authors with the same name.

accepted.x: The pillar bearing the Allahabad Prasasti also carries an inscription of Jahangir, along with Ashoka’s edicts and the Queen’s edict.
accepted.tq: Identify the inscription by location and avoid confusing separate monuments.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly contrasts the messages associated with the inscriptions on the Allahabad pillar?
o: The Allahabad Prasasti glorifies war, whereas Ashoka’s message on the same pillar emphasises peace.
The Allahabad Prasasti advocates Buddhism, whereas Ashoka’s edicts glorify military conquest.
Both the Allahabad Prasasti and Ashoka’s edicts reject warfare in identical terms.
Both inscriptions are primarily commercial records concerning trade routes.
accepted.x: The Allahabad Prasasti celebrates Samudragupta’s military conquests, while Ashoka’s inscriptions on the same pillar convey a message associated with peace and dhamma.
accepted.tq: Use the reversed-comparison trap to distinguish the tone and purpose of the two inscriptions.

The Motupalli charter of the Kakatiyas
